item.title: [ZEPPELIN-101] Need button to save paragraph text changes without executing
item.description: I'm using the Zeppelin "%sql" interpreter to run SQL through the Spark Hive Context. If I make edits to the comments in my SQL, and then change to another notebook, my edits go unsaved. It appears that running the SQL (shift-Enter) is the only way to ensure the text edits are persisted.
item.summary: Need button to save paragraph text changes without executing

status.description: A resolution has been taken, and it is awaiting verification by reporter. From here issues are either reopened, or are closed.

comments.comment: I've been bitten by the same issue. Should it have some sort of periodic saving? Or should it prompt you to save before you navigate away?

Currently a workaround could be collapse and expend code area. that action will saves your code changes without run it.

Until now, Zeppelin tried to not have save button for simplicity of use.

I think we can solve the problem with

  • periodic saving
  • automatic save when closing browser
  • notification when there're unsaved changes
  • save button.
Thanks for the tip to use the collapse/expand workaround. The list of proposed solutions looks good!
It looks like these to are related. having periodic save and save before any other operation such as move paragraph or change notebook would solve both
I'm working on this issue by adding save button to paragrpah

Graying out the button would probably make more sense than hiding it or even making it a no-op. The reason for this is that when you click the Save button, you're going to want to see some feedback that tells you that it was in fact saved. Graying out the button would do this.

If the notebook saved button is only used to save dirty queries, then it becomes pretty useless with the auto save:

Considering the autosave every 10s, I doubt somebody will use the note save button (he could use shortcut or wait) and 10s is pretty short. Auto save would probably kick before you reach the button 50% of the time.

Also, it will probably never save more than one paragraph each time (because of 10s auto save).

Having a dirty feedback on paragraph and an outdated feedback on the result is way enough with auto save.

The only drawback with auto save could be query history in case you do wrong changes.
